intended_object: The affine point (x, y) of an elliptic curve W over a ring R, built from just the fact that (x, y) satisfies the Weierstrass equation. On an elliptic curve, every solution of the equation is automatically nonsingular. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition builds `Point.some x y h'`. The nonsingularity proof `h'` comes from `equation_iff_nonsingular`, which holds because the discriminant Δ of an elliptic curve is a unit. So the result is exactly the affine point (x, y) of W(R). This is the standard fact that, on a smooth Weierstrass curve, a point only has to satisfy the equation.

The generality is right. It works over any commutative ring R with `IsElliptic`, where Δ is a unit. The `Nontrivial R` hypothesis is the one the underlying lemma needs, and it is harmless.

This is a convenience constructor on top of Mathlib's general `Point.some`. It does not narrow any notion.
